item.title: Add My Supplied Voiceover

exact_text: Make mornings easier: prepare your clothes, pack your bag, and plan breakfast the night before. Start tomorrow with less stress.

turns.text: Add a warm, clear English voice-over to this silent clip, saying exactly: “Make mornings easier: prepare your clothes, pack your bag, and plan breakfast the night before. Start tomorrow with less stress.” Keep the video unchanged. No music or captions.

item.tests: Tests adding an exact supplied narration to existing footage rather than returning standalone speech or regenerating the video.

must_haves: The deliverable is the attached kitchen-table video with an audible voice-over, not an audio-only file.
The narration says the supplied script exactly, without omissions, substitutions, or extra spoken words.
The entire narration is intelligible and finishes before the 10-second video ends.
The original footage, framing, and sequence remain unchanged.
There is no music or added on-screen text.

turns.text: add a voice to this clip

dialog.agent:
I can add a voice, but first I need a few details:

1. **What should the voice say?** Send me the exact words.
2. **Do you have a recording?** If you have an audio file of the voice saying those words, attach it. I'll sync the person's lips in your clip to it. This works best and keeps your video exactly as it is.
3. **If you don't have a recording**, describe the voice you want (for example, "a warm, calm man's voice" or "an upbeat young woman"). I can make one from your text, but this changes the video more. On the free plan it may not keep your clip exactly as it is. If that happens, I'll tell you before using any credits.
4. **Is the voice the person on screen talking, or a narrator heard over the clip?**
dialog.why: The reply asks the user for the script, a recording or a voice description, and whether it's on-screen speech or narration, then waits for the answers.
dialog.user: it should say "Make mornings easier: prepare your clothes, pack your bag, and plan breakfast the night before. Start tomorrow with less stress."

dialog.agent:
Thanks, I have the script. Before I use any credits, I need two more answers:

1. **Do you have a recording of someone reading this line?** If so, attach it. I'll sync the person's lips in your clip to it, and the rest of your video stays the same.

2. **If you don't have a recording, what should the voice sound like?** For example, "a warm, calm woman's voice" or "an upbeat young man." I don't have a tool that turns text straight into speech. So I'd make a new short video that reads your line, then take its voice for your clip. That costs more credits, and how well it works depends on your clip.

Also, **is this the person on screen talking, or a narrator heard over the clip?**

The line is about 10 seconds long when read aloud. If your clip is shorter than that, the end of the line will be cut off. Tell me if you'd rather shorten it.
dialog.why: The assistant asks for a recording or a voice description, whether the speaker is on screen or a narrator, and whether to shorten the line. It waits for these answers before using any credits.
dialog.user: no recording. warm and clear voice, you can pick man or woman

turns.agent:
I couldn't add the voice yet because your Magic Hour account doesn't have enough credits. Nothing was made and no credits were used.

**What I did:** I checked your clip and found one person on screen, so I planned for that person to say the line. Since you don't have a recording, I tried to make a short 10-second speaking video from their face, reading your script word for word. The plan was to take its voice and sync your clip's lip movements to it. The account refused that first step.

**Ways to go ahead:**
1. **Add credits** (buy a credit pack or upgrade your plan), and I'll run the same steps unchanged.
2. **Record the line yourself**, on your phone is fine, and attach the audio. Then I only need the lip-sync step, which costs less (about 1 credit per frame of video). It might still need more credits than you have, though.
3. **Shorten the line**, for example to just "Make mornings easier. Start tomorrow with less stress." That needs fewer seconds of voice and fewer credits, but I can't promise it will fit your current balance.

Which would you like to do?
